name: B-Right Realestate Limited
summary: B-Right Realestate Limited has real Mumbai redevelopment activity, sharply higher reported FY26 earnings, and a verified ₹143.45 crore Keystone FSI/PTC agreement. Those positives do not yet establish an investable equity proposition. The FY26 audited statements contain unresolved cash-flow, fixed-asset and ageing inconsistencies; project cash rights, completion costs and lender availability are not reconciled. At the last recovered trade of ₹915 on 16 October, market equity is ₹945.30 crore, versus ₹176.38 crore owner book equity. The requested 19 October close was not recovered. This is a research hold, not a finding of fraud or default. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS are NS because specific material factors are unscoreable, not because all property developers or SME shares are excluded.

GOV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Promoter pledges cover 23.23% of issued capital; broad group advances make minority oversight material.
Cash-flow, PPE and ageing conflicts persist in the revised report, while employee authorizations can add 15% to shares.

GOV.contrary_evidence: The audit opinion is unmodified, CMD pay is unchanged at ₹0.60 crore, and transaction terms and voting outcomes are disclosed. Regulatory review is not a finding of issuer fraud.
GOV.reason: Material disclosure opacity and stewardship risk support 4. Allegations are not treated as convictions or an automatic G1 failure.

MOAT.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: The rating records 10.37 lakh square feet completed and sold, supporting local execution capability.
The signed Keystone FSI/PTC agreement validates an institutional commercialization route.

MOAT.contrary_evidence: No sustained pricing premium, structural cost advantage or independently measured market share was verified; larger Mumbai competitors can bid for the same opportunities.
MOAT.reason: Local relationships and redevelopment skills are useful but do not yet demonstrate durable excess-return barriers.

REV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Six reported years show sales rising from ₹0.3761 crore to ₹167.7942 crore, with latest growth of 62.23%.
Presales and collections, including H1 FY27, support commercial expansion.

REV.contrary_evidence: Changing consolidation, acquisitions, early financing income and project recognition obscure comparable underlying demand.
REV.reason: Reported five/three-year CAGRs are disclosed, not scored as organic. The reliable underlying basis cannot be established, so REV is NS rather than an undisclosed haircut or a high score based on distorted percentages.

DUR.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Eleven ongoing projects and Mumbai redevelopment demand provide an accessible multi-year work base.
The signed Keystone transaction and H1 collection growth support near-term demand.

DUR.contrary_evidence: All projects are regionally concentrated; Ambika represents 52.58% of unrecognized revenue; pipeline projects are not all approved and funded.
DUR.reason: The runway is real but has material concentration, approval and execution constraints; no score is awarded for headline TAM.

CAP.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Owner equity rose from ₹137.1967 crore in FY23 to ₹176.3845 crore in FY26; reported FY26 ROE is 22.13%.
Inventory, financial advances, new entities and remaining project commitments dominate incremental capital use.

CAP.contrary_evidence: Latest profit and presales may reflect genuine value creation, but mature project returns cannot be separated from recognition timing.
CAP.reason: Three/five-year incremental ROIC and project IRR are NS because cost, ownership and capital timing are not matched. Unknown economics are not assigned a neutral or automatically weak score.

CASH.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Reported FY24–FY26 CFO is negative ₹54.4339 crore versus ₹55.2787 crore group PAT.
Removing only short-term borrowing movements gives negative ₹96.3474 crore; even reversing both interest-classification effects would not make that cumulative figure positive.

CASH.contrary_evidence: FY26 collections of ₹124.24 crore and H1 FY27 collections of ₹111.77 crore are favorable; property cash flows are cohort-dependent and lumpy.
CASH.reason: Weak multi-year cash realization and financing movements within CFO support 3. The fully corrected cash ratio remains NS; no intent to mislead is inferred.

BAL.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: March debt is ₹187.2117 crore against cash ₹6.1194 crore, including ₹74.3065 crore current debt and demand/renewal exposure.
Fresh deposit acceptance and renewals were discontinued; group guarantees and unquantified project claims remain.

BAL.contrary_evidence: Owner book equity is ₹176.3845 crore, the rating describes Adequate projected liquidity, and reported collections improved.
BAL.reason: Immediate liquidity and refinancing exposure are material despite asset backing. G3 is unresolved, not proved default.

EXEC.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Infomerics records 10.37 lakh square feet completed/sold, and the Keystone agreement is dated and specific.
FY26 presales and later H1 collections show commercial progress.

EXEC.contrary_evidence: Occupancy/completion certificates for the August/October/December 2026 project targets were not independently verified by the cutoff; pipeline ambitions are not delivery.
EXEC.reason: Verified progress and unverified deadline completion support a mixed 5. Absence of a certificate in retrieved sources is not proof of a delay.

EARN.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Owner PAT in FY23–FY26 is ₹1.9097/2.4300/1.6921/35.1463 crore, a sharply lumpy series.
FY26 PBT is ₹59.0962 crore with other income ₹2.1318 crore, but minority profit of ₹10.4126 crore and PPE/cash-flow conflicts complicate attributable normalization.

EARN.contrary_evidence: Most FY26 reported PBT is not labelled non-operating; EPS ₹34.02 and commercial growth are positive.
EARN.reason: Recognition, margins and normalization cannot be established reliably enough for EARN. This does not deny the reported profit.

R.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: The five-year project runoff settles opening claims without assuming uncommitted finance has been received.
Base/bear cash arithmetic needs shadow rescue; CTC, ownership, escrow and advance partitions remain unverified.

R.contrary_evidence: The bull sensitivity needs no new cash funding, and the omitted future pipeline may have value; neither establishes full equity fair value.
R.reason: Ordinary IRR and R are NS because material project economics are unknown, not because a low supported return is unscoreable. Shadow rescue returns are not used against the 15% hurdle.

D.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Owner book equity ₹176.3845 crore is only 18.66% of the ₹945.3048 crore reference market value.
A 20% noncash book-asset haircut leaves ₹79.4683 crore owner equity, while a 40% haircut leaves zero after liabilities and NCI are counted once.

D.contrary_evidence: Book cost omits development upside; signed contracts, collections and positive equity can mitigate losses.
D.reason: The arithmetic demonstrates material asset and funding sensitivity, not forecast bankruptcy or a guaranteed recovery floor.

P.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: A 15% five-year hurdle requires ₹1,901.3456 crore terminal equity before possible 15% share dilution.
At 15× terminal owner earnings, PAT must reach ₹126.7564 crore, a 29.25% CAGR; at 10×, it must reach ₹190.1346 crore, a 40.16% CAGR.

P.contrary_evidence: Project scale and H1 bookings offer a route; maintaining a 25× exit multiple reduces the required PAT CAGR to 16.69%.
P.reason: Several favorable assumptions must coincide: attributable margins, cash conversion, funding and exit valuation. Reverse P/E is a diagnostic, not project NAV or an estimated probability.

L.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: The eligible lot is 200 shares, costing ₹183,000 at the stale ₹915 reference; ₹5 lakh is not an exact number of lots.
Only 51 of 60 market sessions were recovered; nine missing observations are not confirmed zero trades.

L.contrary_evidence: Observed trades and the lower lot size provide some access; absent records do not prove untradeability.
L.reason: Formal 60-day lower-of-mean/median turnover is unverified. Whole-lot sensitivities are retained, but L remains NS rather than using an invalid mean-based score.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: B-Right Realestate Limited has real Mumbai redevelopment activity, sharply higher reported FY26 earnings, and a verified ₹143.45 crore Keystone FSI/PTC agreement. Those positives do not yet establish an investable equity proposition. The FY26 audited statements contain unresolved cash-flow, fixed-asset and ageing inconsistencies; project cash rights, completion costs and lender availability are not reconciled. At the last recovered trade of ₹915 on 16 October, market equity is ₹945.30 crore, versus ₹176.38 crore owner book equity. The requested 19 October close was not recovered. This is a research hold, not a finding of fraud or default. BQS, Growth Quality GQS and IAS are NS because specific material factors are unscoreable, not because all property developers or SME shares are excluded.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: The exact issuer is B-RIGHT REALESTATE LIMITED, CIN L70100MH2007PLC282631, BSE SME 543543, symbol BRRL, ISIN INE0IZQ01016. It is not another similarly named B-Right group entity. Incorporated in 2007 and formerly Marshal Vinimay Limited, the company operates through several corporate and partnership subsidiaries. Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Financial baseline: consolidated Indian GAAP (Accounting Standards / AS) under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, not Ind AS; year ended 31 March 2026. Basic shares are 10,331,200, face value ₹10. The official 19 October eligible SM security-master row specifies a 200-share lot; the legacy ineligible ST row of 400 is not the current executable lot. G1 is Conditional; G2, G3 and G4 are Hold — unresolved. Identity confidence is High, reported-statement transcription is High, economic comparability and full project valuation are Low. The latest H1 operating release was recovered as mirrored issuer text, not audited interim accounts.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Supported diagnostic factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, DUR 6, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5, D 3 and P 4. REV, CAP, EARN, R and L are NS. BQS has 76% weighted coverage, known contribution 3.22 and exact bounds 3.46–5.62; GQS has 30% coverage, contribution 1.50 and bounds 2.20–8.50. IAS has 30% directly known coverage; propagating the BQS factor-level range gives 2.315–6.905, not a point score. Original weights are retained, with no neutral-five insertion or renormalization. Decimal arithmetic and half-up display produce BQS 3.5–5.6, GQS 2.2–8.5 and IAS 2.3–6.9 bounds. These raw bounds are information-coverage ranges, not confidence intervals or rankings. No G1 or G3 failure cap is imposed. Because CASH 3 reflects weak multi-year realization, the growth-quality cap of 5 applies; its effect on the GQS missing-data range is 2.20–5.00, while the score itself remains NS. Quality ranking was considered independently of IAS; it fails here on missing REV/CAP/EARN, not a blanket G3 exclusion.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The group develops residential and commercial property, especially Mumbai society redevelopment and slum-rehabilitation projects. It also has finance, leasing and construction activities and uses LLPs, partnerships and companies as project vehicles. Buyers pay against booking and construction milestones; reported percentage-completion revenue, presales, cash collections and GDV are different measures. Land can be privately owned, government/SRA land, society redevelopment rights or joint-venture access. Tenant rehabilitation, consent, approvals, title and partner rights are therefore essential costs and constraints, not incidental paperwork. The parent owns 99.9% of B-Right Realestate Ventures LLP; some other entities are consolidated despite lower legal equity percentages, including Farewell at 39.93% and Bhagya at 50%. Consolidated project assets and profits do not all belong to listed shareholders. Parent LLP profit distributions must not be added again to group income. Project-specific land deeds, consent/approval conditions, RERA escrow release rights and economic waterfalls were not independently verified in this pass.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is local redevelopment sourcing, negotiation and execution: experience helps secure societies, coordinate rehabilitation and market completed units. Infomerics records 10.37 lakh square feet completed and sold; the Keystone transaction provides a concrete institutional monetization route. These facts demonstrate capability, not an independently measured market share, enduring pricing premium or superior project IRR. A capable competing developer can recruit similar teams, bid for redevelopment and obtain bank/project finance; site-specific rights can create temporary scarcity while also exposing the holder to disputes. Economic peers are Arkade, Keystone/Rustomjee and Sunteck, not identical P/E comparables. Arkade reported FY26 presales ₹901 crore and collections ₹728 crore. Keystone reported Q1 FY27 presales ₹617 crore, collections ₹599 crore, net debt ₹72.8 crore and separately identified its ₹90.8 crore share of JV debt. Sunteck’s older 9M FY26 release reported presales ₹2,093 crore, collections ₹1,001 crore and net operating cash surplus ₹349 crore. Periods, scale, portfolio mix and accounting differ. Their useful benchmark is explicit project cash and claim disclosure, not a borrowed valuation multiple or a claim that size alone creates a moat.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: Reported consolidated operating sales for FY21–FY26 are ₹0.3761/0.7600/17.2181/40.8958/103.4314/167.7942 crore. Annual additions are ₹0.3839/16.4581/23.6777/62.5356/64.3628 crore. Mechanical five-year CAGR is 238.7% and three-year CAGR 113.6%; latest FY26 growth is 62.23%. The extremely small early recognized-sales base, financing/investment income, new entities and project recognition make those rates unsuitable as a verified organic growth score. There is no defensible ten-year or current financial TTM series in this packet. FY26 presales of ₹286.4 crore compare with ₹186 crore and ₹97 crore in FY25/FY24. Collections were ₹124.24 crore, but collections cannot be compared with only same-year presales as a cash-conversion ratio because customers pay across project cohorts. The 16 October release mirror reports H1 FY27 presales ₹235.88 crore and collections ₹111.77 crore, versus ₹84.39 crore and ₹25.26 crore. These are favorable operating signals, not a substitute for an interim P&L, organic bridge or project-cohort reconciliation. REV remains NS rather than assigning a misleading high score from reported CAGR.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The FY26 presentation lists 11 ongoing projects with projected gross revenue ₹1,840 crore and 19 upcoming projects with ₹7,546 crore potential GDV. Ongoing saleable area is 753,712 square feet, with 394,740 sold. Ambika Nagar accounts for ₹867 crore of the ₹1,649 crore unrecognized-revenue total, about 52.6%; this is materially concentrated. Expected completions range from August/October/December 2026 to December 2029, but current occupancy/completion certificates were not recovered. The June agreement contemplates ₹143.452062 crore for 176 FSI/PTC units at Ambika; payment milestones and attributable margin are not disclosed, and it is not added again to the same ₹951 crore project GDV. August’s Bhagat Singh Nagar MoU indicates ₹1,600 crore potential GDV, not a completed, approved and funded acquisition. Tattva & Mittal cost ₹1 lakh for 100%, September Highlines increased from 49% to 80% for ₹31,000, and the October township incorporation mirror records an 80% ₹80,000 subscription. Nominal equity prices do not bound inherited project obligations. Three new H1 sites and planned launches are opportunities, not automatic equity NAV. Capital efficiency is NS because full costs, timing and attributable project rights cannot be matched to capital deployed.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text: Sanjay Nathalal Shah is Chairman and Managing Director; promoters include Cheerful Dealtrade LLP and Blow Sales LLP. June promoter ownership is 73.15%; 2.4 million shares are encumbered, 23.23% of total capital and 31.76% of promoter shares. A March event increased Malani Ventures’ HDFC-pledged shares by 770,000 to 1,630,000. CMD remuneration stayed ₹60 lakh; reimbursement fell from ₹69.37 lakh to ₹7.62 lakh. Ayekart Foundation received ₹50.50 lakh CSR in the related-party disclosure. Loans/advances and group entities require transaction-level reconciliation rather than presuming every related balance is abuse. JMMK & Co issued an unmodified audit opinion, relying on other auditors for substantial subsidiary balances; no adverse resignation was established. Infomerics’ 14 May watch-negative action follows media-reported regulatory review of Khot Dongri involving joint-development partner Shah Housecon. It expressly says the impact is uncertain. This is not a conviction, proven issuer fraud or proof that similarly named individuals are the same person. A specific company reconciliation/response resolving that exposure was not located in the retrieved filings. Favorable evidence includes completed projects, disclosed commercial agreements and adequate projected coverage in the rating rationale. On 14 August shareholders approved discontinuing new/renewed public deposits while retaining existing repayment obligations. They also authorized 1,033,120 ESOPs and 516,560 performance units, potentially 15% of present shares. Grants/exercises were not verified; no exercise proceeds are booked.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 reported revenue is ₹167.7942 crore, PBT ₹59.0962 crore, group PAT before minority ₹45.5867 crore and owner PAT ₹35.1463 crore. Core EBITDA reconstructed as PBT + interest + depreciation − other income is ₹65.6315 crore, but an industrial EBITDA multiple is not used to value property inventory. FY25 PBT before the ₹2.6457 crore extraordinary item is ₹11.0306 crore; its cash-flow disposal-gain label/sign is unresolved, so normalized PAT is NS. Owner PAT for FY23–FY26 was ₹1.9097/2.4300/1.6921/35.1463 crore; the FY26 jump is not assumed repeatable. Reported three-year CFO totals negative ₹54.4339 crore against group PAT ₹55.2787 crore. The cash-flow statement includes short-term borrowing changes in operations and positive interest expense in financing. Removing only short-term borrowing movement gives FY24/FY25/FY26 negative ₹122.3630/positive ₹49.4818/negative ₹23.4662 crore; these are narrow diagnostics, not certified corrected CFO. Cash taxes are blank while tax provisions rise; zero cash tax cannot be assumed. Gross cash capex/FCF cannot be isolated reliably from the net disposal line and inconsistent PPE schedule. At March, cash is ₹6.1194 crore; debt ₹187.2117 crore; WIP ₹159.3277 crore; receivables ₹57.8268 crore; loans/advances ₹141.1204 crore; investments ₹67.4022 crore; noncurrent deposits ₹34.002 crore. These last assets are not all free cash. PPE net block differs by ₹10.0527 crore between note and balance sheet, depreciation differs, receivable-age labels conflict, and the payable-ageing total includes an unexplained ₹31.2239 crore beyond the balance-sheet balance. Images confirm these are present in the document. The July revision corrected voting only. Both favorable audited earnings and the unresolved data defects remain in view.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text: The ₹915 last observed 16 October price implies ₹945.3048 crore equity, 26.90 times FY26 owner PAT and 5.36 times owner book equity. None is a current executable quote. Sector-appropriate value must follow project receipts minus remaining construction, rehabilitation/landholder costs, tax, debt and partner claims, plus genuinely separate realizable assets. The presentation’s ₹405 crore receivables plus ₹1,279 crore unsold value totals ₹1,684 crore, whereas GDV less ₹185 crore receipts is ₹1,655 crore; the ₹29 crore gap and individual project contradictions prevent a supported NAV. The attached five-year FY27–FY31 runoff uses the lower ₹1,655 crore only as a diagnostic cash proxy, realization 75/90/100%, remaining cash costs ₹1,050/850/650 crore, separately settled opening claims, explicit NCI and 25% illustrative new-profit cash tax. These costs and rights are hypotheses, not signed budgets. Current debt is settled in FY27; remaining LT debt is deducted at terminal. Shadow rescue financing of ₹600.41/163.75/zero crore is required in bear/base/bull cash arithmetic and is never labelled available. Resulting shadow terminal prices ₹0/81.78/400.35 are incomplete existing-portfolio sensitivities, not fair values, because other asset recovery, rights and project costs remain unknown. Ordinary equity returns are therefore withheld in all cases. The full 15% employee pool, if issued without credited exercise cash, divides terminal per-share values by 1.15. A 15% five-year hurdle requires ₹1,901.35 crore terminal equity or ₹1,840.39 per basic share; a reverse 15× owner-PAT assumption requires ₹126.76 crore profit, 29.25% annual growth from FY26. At 10×/20×/25× the required PAT is ₹190.13/95.07/76.05 crore. These reverse expectations are not assigned probabilities or imported peer multiples.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A credible loss path is delayed approvals or disputed development rights, slower milestone collections, construction/rehabilitation inflation and demand-linked refinancing while pledged shares fall. Ambika concentration and Khot Dongri uncertainty make this more than a generic cyclical warning, but neither establishes actual default. All gross property value is subject to lenders, statutory taxes, tenants/landholders and partners before common equity. A 20% haircut to all noncash book assets, holding recorded liabilities and NCI fixed, leaves ₹79.47 crore owner equity; a 40% haircut leaves zero. This is a recovery diagnostic, not a fair-value appraisal, and book values can omit development upside. The restraint test removes all discretionary future pipeline spending, retains existing-project completion and known completed acquisitions, and does not impose an invented cash buffer or mechanical maintenance schedule. It still cannot certify survival because usable project cash, CTC and maturity terms are missing. The rating’s funding closure and Adequate projected liquidity are genuine favorable counterevidence. The ₹45 crore group guarantee is not charged again alongside the underlying consolidated debt; disputed-payable and contingent-tax sensitivities are separate unresolved bounds, not stacked as an alleged default.

sections.title: 5× and 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold the reference equity value are ₹4,726.52 crore and ₹9,453.05 crore. Over five years they require annual share-price growth of 37.97% and 58.49%, before any dividends. At an illustrative terminal 15× owner earnings, required annual PAT is ₹315.10 crore or ₹630.20 crore, versus FY26 ₹35.15 crore. Potential issuance of all approved employee pools raises the aggregate profit/value needed for a fixed per-share target by 15%, before any genuine exercise proceeds. Ongoing GDV ₹1,840 crore and future pipeline ₹7,546 crore are gross multi-year sales, not recurring annual profit or equity. Delivery needs legally secure rights, new land/rehabilitation investment, collections, financing, taxes and minority economics. The current packet supports a growth opportunity but not a funded, attributable 5×/10× case. There is no mathematical impossibility claim; the missing proof is cash economics and execution, not the size of the headline pipeline.

sections.title: Liquidity and Implementation
sections.text: A 200-share lot costs ₹183,000 at the stale ₹915 reference. ₹5 lakh cannot be represented exactly: two lots are ₹366,000 and three ₹549,000. The 60 exchange-session window through 19 October contains only 51 recovered secondary observations; nine missing sessions cannot be treated as proven zero trades. The 20-session window has 14 observations. Consequently actual 60-day mean/median turnover and formal L are NS. As an explicitly hypothetical zero-missing sensitivity, low×volume gives 60-day mean ₹31.71734 lakh and median ₹14.8599 lakh; use the lower median, not the larger mean. ₹5 lakh continuous exits at 2/5/10% participation are 16.82/6.73/3.36 sessions. Daily whole-lot flooring is more restrictive: the same 60-day sensitivity yields 7/36/93 lots in total and only 3/18/29 days with capacity for even one lot at 2/5/10%. Median capacity is zero lots for all three rates. The latest observed day traded only 200 shares, so selling one lot would be 100% of that day’s volume, not 5%. OHLC×volume bounds are not actual traded value; no spread, executable depth, circuit-lock history or current surveillance clearance was verified. Do not present this reference size as suitable for any particular investor.

sections.title: Key Uncertainties, Counterevidence and Monitoring
sections.text: Highest-priority evidence is a management/auditor reconciliation of CFO, interest/tax classification, PPE and both ageing schedules; project-level remaining cash budgets and signed commitment schedules; land/rehabilitation/RERA escrow rights; and parent-attributable project waterfalls. Obtain a current consolidated debt and usable-cash reconciliation, especially the October release’s ₹120 crore debt claim versus March’s ₹187.21 crore, rather than calling it deleveraging on unmatched scopes. Verify unused sanctioned limits, deposit maturity runoff after scheme closure, guarantee overlap and the liquidity/recovery of investments, advances and deposits. Recover September shareholding, actual ESOP/PSU grants and market data for the nine missing sessions plus the requested 19 October quote. Check OC/completion outcomes for Shrishti, Anand and Nirvana without assuming absence equals delay. Monitor Khot Dongri for primary regulatory/court records and a specific company response; credit watch is not a legal verdict. Positives that could change the conclusion are independently reconciled cash generation, resolved title/approval exposure, signed funded CTC with partner economics, sustained collections and documented release of capital. No external contact or recurring monitoring was initiated.

sections.title: Final Investment View and Decision Rules
sections.text: Keep this issuer on a verification watchlist, outside provisional score rankings until the material NS factors can be resolved. Do not buy solely because reported FY26 PAT rose sharply, a marquee counterparty signed an agreement, or projected GDV exceeds market capitalization. Equally, do not reject it as fraudulent or insolvent based on document errors, unproven allegations or a deliberately conservative sensitivity. A supported investment view needs a reconciled project-to-equity cash model and a dated executable price, followed by a base return above the 15% hurdle with a funded downside. The work is reproducible from saved primary PDFs, extracts, raw secondary observations, exact input/evidence ledgers, claims ledger and model code. The valuation outputs are labelled diagnostic, and all three composite scores remain NS. All comparisons and any future rankings remain provisional until the full research universe is complete.

gates.reason: Promoter encumbrance, complex advances and disclosure inconsistencies require scrutiny. The Khot Dongri regulatory review concerns a joint-development arrangement; allegations are not findings of issuer fraud. No evidenced integrity disqualification established.

Unmodified opinion is favorable, but primary cash-flow financing classifications, PPE/depreciation, receivable ageing and trade-payable totals conflict. July correction addresses voting only. Some facts and factors remain usable; capital efficiency, underlying growth and earnings normalization are critically unresolved.

Project CTC, ownership/escrow, debt maturity and genuinely undrawn signed availability are unverified. Rating identifies a funded project and Adequate liquidity, but does not prove full-portfolio funding. Deposit scheme closed for fresh/renewed deposits. The BSE SME eligible 200-share lot is verified. Nine of 60 market sessions are missing, the 19 October print is unavailable, and depth/circuit/surveillance status is unverified. This prevents a supported execution conclusion; effective untradeability is not proved.

score_note: Supported diagnostic factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, DUR 6, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5, D 3 and P 4. REV, CAP, EARN, R and L are NS. BQS has 76% weighted coverage, known contribution 3.22 and exact bounds 3.46–5.62; GQS has 30% coverage, contribution 1.50 and bounds 2.20–8.50. IAS has 30% directly known coverage; propagating the BQS factor-level range gives 2.315–6.905, not a point score. Original weights are retained, with no neutral-five insertion or renormalization. Decimal arithmetic and half-up display produce BQS 3.5–5.6, GQS 2.2–8.5 and IAS 2.3–6.9 bounds. These raw bounds are information-coverage ranges, not confidence intervals or rankings. No G1 or G3 failure cap is imposed. Because CASH 3 reflects weak multi-year realization, the growth-quality cap of 5 applies; its effect on the GQS missing-data range is 2.20–5.00, while the score itself remains NS. Quality ranking was considered independently of IAS; it fails here on missing REV/CAP/EARN, not a blanket G3 exclusion.
